# sagp pilot: per-gradient cost, fit diagnostics and the alpha table

**Provenance.** Generated by `--stage grad` under `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
XLA_FLAGS="--xla_cpu_multi_thread_eigen=false intra_op_parallelism_threads=1"`, with the
post-R38 module. These single-thread per-gradient times agree with the multi-threaded
`--stage grad` table in the main pilot file
(`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-sagp-pilot.md`) within 20% (n = 200: 4.36 vs 4.32 ms
product/lengthscale, 45 vs 44.6 ms additive/amplitude, 198 vs 196 ms additive/lengthscale, 136
vs 133 ms product/amplitude), so the isolated gradient was effectively single-threaded
already, and hours derived from it are core-hours.

Generated by `scripts/pilot_sagp.py` (plan task 11). Each section is written by its own stage and
carries the date, host and core count of the run that produced it, so sections may come from
different runs; `--stage all` refreshes all of them. Regenerate with

```
PYTHONPATH=. /opt/anaconda3/envs/saasbo/bin/python scripts/pilot_sagp.py --stage all
```

(on a laptop, under `caffeinate -di`: a sleeping machine does not advance `perf_counter`, so a
suspended run reports times that are wrong rather than merely late).

## Stage: grad

Measured 2026-09-08 on `CW52D2L07Q`, `os.cpu_count()` = 8.

One jitted gradient of each cell's log-joint at D = 100 (`jax.grad` of
`numpyro.infer.util.log_density` on random standardized data with a learned noise), the
mean of 5 timed calls after one untimed compile call. The fit estimate
is `768 x steps x t_grad` over the 40-63
leapfrog steps per iteration that `max_tree_depth = 6` allows.

| cell | n = 50 | n = 100 | n = 200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| product/lengthscale | 0.28 ms -> 0.143-0.226 min/fit | 1.09 ms -> 0.561-0.883 min/fit | 4.36 ms -> 2.23-3.51 min/fit |
| additive/amplitude | 5.58 ms -> 2.85-4.5 min/fit | 14.1 ms -> 7.21-11.4 min/fit | 45 ms -> 23-36.3 min/fit |
| additive/lengthscale | 7.09 ms -> 3.63-5.71 min/fit | 48.4 ms -> 24.8-39 min/fit | 198 ms -> 101-159 min/fit |
| product/amplitude | 7.25 ms -> 3.71-5.84 min/fit | 24.6 ms -> 12.6-19.8 min/fit | 136 ms -> 69.6-110 min/fit |

The 2026-09-07 measurement this stage reproduces (same laptop, same procedure), for
comparison:

| cell | n = 50 | n = 100 | n = 200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| product/lengthscale | 0.4 ms | 0.5 ms | 3.1 ms |
| additive/amplitude | 7.6 ms | 20.0 ms | 45.0 ms |
| additive/lengthscale | 6.6 ms | 56.0 ms | 173.0 ms |
| product/amplitude | 7.3 ms | 29.0 ms | 135.0 ms |
